To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PVP is a promising cathode buffer layer to enhance the efficiency of P3HT: PCBM BHJ-PSCs, and the efficiency enhancement is attributed to the formation of PVP cathode interlayer via self-assembly or by spin-coating, which leads to a dipole layer formation between P3HT/PCBM active layer, and Al electrode, and chemical reactions of P3HT/ PCBM active layer and PVP cathode layer.

the incorporation of a non-conjugated PVP layer as a cathode interface layer in BHJ-PSCs can enhance the device performance by 29% (spin coating) and 13% (doping), which is attributed to the increase of charge collection efficiency, and that the enhancement of device performance is dependent on the aggregation microstructure of PVP cathode interface layer.

the incorporation of a poly(vinyl pyrrolidone)(PVP) layer by either spin-coating or doping into P3HT:phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester(P3HT:PC61BM) active layer leads to the enhancement of the performance of polymer solar cells (PSCs).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the application of PVP as a new cathodic buffer layer in BHJ-PSCs via spin coating or doping into the P3H:PCBM active layers, and the results indicate that the PCE of the BHJ-PSC devices could be enhanced by applying a PVP cathodic buffer layer via spin-coating or self-assembly.
a novel PVP cathode interlayer in BHJ-PSCs, which leads to an enhancement in device performance.
the development of a new cathode interlayer for BHJ-PSCs by means of spin coating or self-assembling, resulting in the significant enhancement of PCE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PCE enhancement is due to the conjunct effects, which include the formation of the dipole layer, the chemical reactions between the PVP layer and Al electrodes and the increase of roughness of the Al film.
the formation of the thin PVP cathode interlayer by self-assembly is a more effective approach to improve the performance of BHJ-PSCs.

PVP is a very promising cathode buffer layer for BHJ-PSCs, and the efficiency enhancement of BHJ-PSC devices is attributed to the formation of the dipole layer between the P3HT/PCBM active layer (donor) and Al electrodes (acceptor) and to the chemical reaction between PVP and Al.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PVP cathodes formed by self- or spin-coating can enhance the device efficiency of the BHJ-PSCs, but the PVP cathodic formed by self- assembly can enhance the device performance better than that formed by spin coating, because the PVP molecules can be self-assembled into the PVP interlayers with a better aggregation microstructure.
the PVP cathodic buffer layer is a promising material for the fabrication of high performance BHJ-PSCs.
the incorporation of PVP layer as a cathode interlayer by either spin coating or doping can be used as a general strategy to improve the performance of polymer solar cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

PVP can be used to form a cathode buffer interlayer in BHJ-PSCs, and the PVP cathodic buffer layer is beneficial to the enhancement of the performance of the device, which can be achieved by either spin coating or doping PVP into the active layer.

the PVP cathodes can be fabricated via either self-assembly or the spin-coating method, and the PVP cathodic buffer layer formed by either method is beneficial to the performance enhancement of the P3HT-based BHJ-PSCs.
the PVP interlayers can be formed via self-assembly or via spin coating, resulting in significant enhancement of the device efficiency.
